title: Permissionless honeypot registry for Arc pools
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet holding an append-only, permissionless registry of attestations about liquidity pools. Anyone may attest that a given pool address is predatory, attaching the evidence on chain: the pool's own fee() reading and its USDC balance, both read by the contract itself at attestation time rather than supplied by the attester. This is grounded in measured fact: a scan of 4,000 Arc blocks on 2026-09-17 found Uniswap V4 pools configured with 97%, 99%, 88% and 32% fees holding under a thousandth of a dollar, which drain any router that touches them, sitting alongside legitimate pools for the same token. The contract verifies what it can (fee, balance) and records what it cannot (intent) as an attributed opinion, so the registry never claims an authority it does not have. Routers and front-ends can read it before routing.

title: Exact self-refunding calls, denominated in the gas asset itself
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet that lets a sponsor pre-fund an allowance, then refunds a caller the exact cost of the call they just made, measured as gasUsed multiplied by tx.gasprice inside the transaction. The refund is paid in the same asset the gas was paid in, because on Arc the gas token is USDC. On every other EVM chain this primitive requires an ETH/USD oracle and always over- or under-refunds by the oracle's error and staleness; the sponsor must over-collateralise and the user bears basis risk. On Arc the refund is exact and oracle-free by construction. The contract enforces per-call and per-sponsor ceilings, a per-caller rate limit, and an allowance that the sponsor can revoke, so a drained sponsor is impossible rather than merely unlikely.

title: On-chain record of cross-venue price deviation
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet that records, permissionlessly, when two liquidity pools for the same token pair quote prices that differ by more than their combined fees. The caller names two pools; the contract reads slot0 from each, reads each pool's USDC balance as a depth measure, computes the deviation and the fee barrier itself, and stores the result only if the deviation genuinely clears the barrier. Nothing is taken on the caller's word. It turns an ephemeral market condition into a durable public record, which is what a researcher or a market maker actually wants and what no explorer provides. Measured context: on 2026-09-17 the only Arc pair with two liquid venues, cirBTC/USDC, never cleared its 0.053% fee barrier across 200 consecutive blocks.

title: A vault that refuses to lose value to the 18/6 truncation
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet that accepts native USDC deposits at 18 decimals and issues claims tracked at the 6 decimals the ERC-20 predeploy reports, refusing any deposit or withdrawal whose amount would be silently truncated by the 1e12 factor between Arc's two representations of the same balance. Instead of rounding quietly, it reverts with the exact residue, so an integrator discovers the mismatch at the boundary rather than in a slow leak. Arc carries one balance in two views: native at 18 decimals for msg.value and eth_getBalance, and the predeploy at 0x3600...0000 at 6 decimals, related by exactly 1e12. Assuming 6 decimals for the native asset overstates every amount by a trillion, which is the natural mistake because USDC is a 6-decimal token on every other chain.

title: Scheduled and dead-man's-switch payments in native USDC
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet holding funds that release to a named beneficiary on a schedule, or if the depositor fails to check in within a chosen interval. Payments are denominated in native USDC. Useful for inheritance, vesting and operational continuity.

title: An on-chain atlas of Arc's predeploys and canonical infrastructure
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet recording which canonical addresses actually carry bytecode on Arc, refreshed permissionlessly by anyone calling it, so integrators can check from on chain rather than guessing. Measured context: probing canonical addresses on Arc and treating the presence of bytecode as proof that the canonical contract is deployed does not work, because two unrelated canonical addresses returned identical bytecode length and prefix.

title: ArcMeter, already built and deployed (calibration baseline)
text: A contract deployed on Arc Mainnet holding a permissionless, append-only registry of what specific EVM operations cost, measured with gasleft() deltas from inside transactions and published as both a gas count and a dollar amount. Because Arc's gas token is USDC carried at 18 decimals, gasUsed multiplied by tx.gasprice is a dollar amount directly, with no price feed in the expression. The measurement harness is published as its own operation rather than subtracted silently, and cold benchmarks derive their storage slot from a counter so each run genuinely touches an untouched slot.
